name: Dumbbell Overhead Triceps Extension
summary: An isolation exercise that targets the triceps, particularly the long head, by extending the elbows overhead with a dumbbell.

setup: Sit upright on a bench, preferably with low-back support, with your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp a dumbbell vertically with both hands, cupping the underside of the top weight plate in a diamond grip with your palms facing up.
Press the dumbbell directly overhead until your arms are fully extended and your upper arms are close to vertical.
steps: Keeping your upper arms stationary and elbows tucked inward, inhale and bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head in a controlled arc.
Lower the weight until your forearms contact your biceps or you feel a deep stretch in your triceps.
Exhale and contract your triceps to extend your elbows, pressing the dumbbell back to the starting overhead position without locking out forcefully.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you lower the weight behind your head; exhale as you press the dumbbell back overhead.
cues: Keep elbows pointing forward, not flaring wide
Keep your ribs pulled down and spine neutral

common_faults.fault: Excessive elbow flaring outward during the descent.
common_faults.correction: Keep your elbows pulled in so they point forward or slightly diagonal, protecting the shoulder joint and keeping tension on the triceps.

common_faults.fault: Arching the lower back excessively to heave the weight up.
common_faults.correction: Engage your abdominal muscles, brace your core, and reduce the weight if you cannot maintain a neutral spine.

common_faults.fault: Swinging the upper arms forward and back.
common_faults.correction: Lock your upper arms in place beside your head and ensure movement only occurs at the elbow joint.

precautions: Carefully guide the dumbbell to and from your shoulders or lap when initiating and finishing the set to avoid dropping it behind your head.
Ensure a secure two-handed grip on the inside of the dumbbell plate before hoisting it overhead.
